target_condition.notes: Primary conditions investigated in the study

control.notes: Healthy controls represent the control group in this case-control analysis

country.evidence_quote: a cohort of 196 Chinese individuals; Tangshan, a large modern city in northern China
country.notes: Study participants were from China, specifically Tangshan city

body_site.evidence_quote: metagenomic and metabolomic analyses; fecal microbiota; stool samples

days_from_first_collection.notes: This is not a longitudinal study with multiple time points for individual subjects; cross-sectional design

lifestyle.notes: Participants from modern urban setting; traditional/non-westernized categories not applicable

location.evidence_quote: Kailuan community in Tangshan, a large modern city in northern China

probing_pocket_depth.notes: Not applicable; this is a hypertension/microbiota study, not a periodontal study

antibiotics_exclusion_period_unit.notes: Unit of measurement for antibiotic washout period

probing_pocket_depth_value.notes: Not applicable; not a periodontal study

dna_extraction_kit.section: Methods — Stool sample collection and DNA extraction
dna_extraction_kit.notes: TIANGEN kit used for bacterial DNA extraction from stool samples

ncbi_accession.notes: No NCBI SRA/ENA accessions provided in the paper

sequencing_platform.section: Methods — Metagenomic sequencing and gene catalogue construction
sequencing_platform.notes: Illumina platform used for shotgun metagenomic sequencing; HiSeq model inferred from context and standard platform naming

age.notes: Individual-level age data not reported; only study-level aggregates available and age not mentioned as a significant differentiator

age_group.notes: Age group classifications not explicitly provided; participants are adults (employees) but no age stratification reported

age_unit.notes: Not applicable; age data not reported

ancestry.notes: Participants described as Chinese but no detailed ancestry categories provided

ancestry_details.notes: No detailed ancestry terms beyond geographic origin (China/Tangshan) reported

family.notes: Not a family-based sampling design; individual employees from occupational cohort

family_role.notes: Not applicable; not a family-based study

sex.evidence_quote: gender ratio is discrepant among groups
sex.notes: Gender/sex ratios differ between groups but individual-level data not provided; no significant gender effect on bacterial abundance found

zigosity.notes: Twin zygosity not applicable; study involves unrelated cohort members.

age_min.evidence_quote: Male GF mice aged 8–10 weeks were randomly distributed into two groups

age_max.evidence_quote: Male GF mice aged 8–10 weeks were randomly distributed into two groups
age_max.notes: Age range for mouse recipients; human participants' ages not reported.

age_years.notes: Human participant ages not reported in paper; mouse ages reported in weeks.

antibiotics_current_use.evidence_quote: Individuals were also excluded if they had received antibiotics or probiotics within the last 8 weeks.
antibiotics_current_use.section: Results — GM diversity and enterotype in pHTN and HTN
antibiotics_current_use.notes: Exclusion criterion applied to all human study participants.

bmi.notes: Paper states no significant difference in BMI among groups but does not report actual values or ranges.

dietary_restriction.notes: Dietary restrictions not reported; study notes diets were relatively small in differences due to concentrated environment.

disease.evidence_quote: cohort of 41 healthy controls, 56 subjects with pre-hypertension, 99 individuals with primary hypertension
disease.notes: Three disease groups studied; hypertension group composed of newly diagnosed patients.

disease_details.notes: Hypertension subgroup specified as primary hypertension; pre-hypertension not further detailed.

disease_response_pfs.notes: Not applicable; study is observational cohort study without treatment/progression monitoring.

disease_response_pfs_month.notes: Not applicable; observational study without treatment follow-up.

disease_response_recist.notes: Not applicable; RECIST criteria for solid tumors, not hypertension study.

feces_phenotype.notes: Stool samples collected but no specific clinical fecal phenotype measurements (e.g., consistency, color) reported.

fmt_id.notes: Study-specific FMT participant IDs not provided in paper; donors identified in supplementary table only.

fmt_role.evidence_quote: fecal bacteria from hypertensive patients were transplanted to GF mice; fresh fecal samples from donors
fmt_role.section: Results — High BP is transferrable by fecal transplant
fmt_role.notes: Human participants served as donors; germ-free mice as recipients of FMT procedure.

hla.notes: Human leukocyte antigen typing not performed or reported in study.

neonatal_birth_weight.notes: Not applicable; study involves adult human cohort and adult-aged mice, not neonates.

neonatal_delivery_procedure.notes: Not applicable; study does not include neonatal or birth delivery information.

neonatal_feeding_method.notes: Not applicable; study involves adults and mice, not infant feeding methods.

neonatal_gestational_age.notes: Not applicable; no neonatal data reported.

neonatal_preterm_birth.notes: Not applicable; study does not include birth-related outcomes.

obgyn_birth_control.notes: Not reported; gender discrepancy noted among groups but contraceptive use not discussed.

obgyn_lactating.notes: Not reported; no lactation status information provided.

obgyn_menopause.notes: Menopausal status not reported; gender ratio discrepant among groups but details not provided.

obgyn_pregnancy.notes: Not reported; pregnancy status not addressed in study.

smoker.evidence_quote: Patients suffering from cancer, heart failure, renal failure, smoking, stroke were all excluded.
smoker.section: Results — GM diversity and enterotype in pHTN and HTN
smoker.notes: Smoking was an exclusion criterion for all participants.

treatment.evidence_quote: All the subjects in the hypertension group were newly diagnosed hypertensive patients prior to antihypertensive treatment.
treatment.section: Results — GM diversity and enterotype in pHTN and HTN
treatment.notes: No antihypertensive treatment reported; study excluded participants on specific drugs (statins, aspirin, insulin, metformin, nifedipine, metoprolol).

tumor_staging_ajcc.notes: Not applicable; study focuses on hypertension, not cancer staging.

tumor_staging_tnm.notes: Not applicable; TNM staging used for cancer, not hypertension.

biomarker_name.evidence_quote: Prevotella and Klebsiella were overrepresented in individuals with pHTN or HTN. Faecalibacterium, Oscillibacter, Roseburia, Bifidobacterium, Coprococcus, and Butyrivibrio were enriched in healthy controls.
biomarker_name.section: Results — pHTN and HTN-associated genera in GM; Results — Metabolic profiling
biomarker_name.notes: Multiple bacterial genera and metabolites identified as biomarkers for distinguishing hypertensive/pre-hypertensive from healthy controls. These represent both microbial compositional and metabolomic signatures.

biomarker_unit.evidence_quote: The abundance of genes was calculated by counting the number of reads and normalizing by gene length.
biomarker_unit.section: Methods — Metagenomic sequencing and gene catalogue construction
biomarker_unit.notes: Paper reports relative abundances but does not explicitly specify units for all metabolite measurements; LC/MS analysis performed but specific units not detailed for metabolites.

biomarker_value.evidence_quote: 44 genera were differentially enriched in control, pHTN, and HTN (P < 0.1, Wilcoxon rank sum test). Prevotella and Klebsiella were overrepresented; Faecalibacterium and Roseburia declined.
biomarker_value.section: Results — pHTN and HTN-associated genera in GM
biomarker_value.notes: Specific fold-changes or absolute values not always provided; statistical significance reported instead (P-values, Wilcoxon rank sum test).

disease_response_os.notes: Paper focuses on gut microbiota dysbiosis and hypertension pathogenesis; no survival data reported.

disease_response_os_unit.notes: Not applicable; overall survival not measured in this study.

ecog_performance_status.notes: ECOG performance status not assessed in this microbiome/hypertension study.

value: altered KEGG modules for amino acid biosynthesis
increased LPS biosynthesis and export genes
feces_phenotype_value.evidence_quote: Compared to healthy controls, we found dramatically decreased microbial richness and diversity, Prevotella-dominated gut enterotype, distinct metagenomic composition with reduced bacteria associated with healthy status and overgrowth of bacteria such as Prevotella and Klebsiella.
feces_phenotype_value.notes: Comprehensive fecal microbiota phenotypes characterized through shotgun metagenomic sequencing, enterotype classification, and functional annotation.

tumor_size_measurement.notes: Tumor size not relevant; study concerns hypertension and gut microbiota, not oncology.

tumor_size_residual_measurement.notes: Not applicable; no tumor-related measurements in this study.

value: Study cohort: 41 healthy controls, 56 pre-hypertensive subjects, 99 primary hypertension patients from Kailuan Group Corporation employees
Sequencing platform: Illumina, 1211 Gb total with 6.18±1.43 million reads per sample
Fecal microbiota transplantation performed from hypertensive patients to germ-free mice
Blood pressure measured by tail-cuff method at 10 weeks post-transplant
Metabolomic analysis: 124 subjects (30 controls, 31 pHTN, 63 HTN) via LC/MS
Classification performance: AUC 0.91 for HTN vs control, AUC 0.89 for pHTN vs control using CAGs+metabolites
Germ-free mouse recipients of hypertensive microbiota showed elevated SBP (P=0.018), DBP (P=0.019), MBP (P=0.014)
uncurated_metadata.evidence_quote: cohort of 196 Chinese individuals...41 healthy controls, 56 subjects with pHTN, and 99 patients with primary HTN. A total of 1211 Gb 125-bp paired-end reads were generated, with an average of 6.18±1.43 (s.d.) million reads per sample.
uncurated_metadata.notes: Additional study design and outcome data not captured by other structured fields.

host_species.evidence_quote: cohort of 196 Chinese individuals. Male GF mice at 8–10 weeks were divided into groups and orally inoculated with stool samples two times at 1-day interval.
host_species.notes: Study included both human participants (metagenomic and metabolomic analysis) and laboratory mice (fecal microbiota transplantation experiments).

Age reported only for mouse experiments (8-10 weeks) not human participants; human age not explicitly stated or used in microbiota analysis.
Fecal microbiota transplantation experiments used 3 donor samples (1 control, 2 HTN), creating separate mouse cohort; extracted data reflects primarily the human metagenomic cohort (n=196).
Batch 1 returned granularity='subgroup_level', differs from batch 0 ('study_level'); kept batch 0.
Batch 1 subgroups ['healthy controls', 'pre-hypertension', 'hypertension', 'HTN mice (recipient)', 'control mice (recipient)'] differ from batch 0 []; kept batch 0.
Paper reports study cohort characteristics at group level only; individual-level sample data not provided in paper text.
Human participant ages not reported in the paper; only mouse recipient ages (8-10 weeks) specified.
Gender ratio noted as discrepant among groups but specific numbers/percentages not stated in main text.
BMI reported as no significant difference among groups but actual values not provided.
FMT study involved only 3 donors (2 HTN, 1 control) and 11-15 recipient mice total; limited granularity for per-sample reporting.
Exclusion criteria (smoking, certain medications, antibiotics/probiotics within 8 weeks) applied to all human participants; all subgroups meet 'No' for these criteria.
Schema field 'disease_response_os' is not applicable to this microbiome-hypertension mechanistic study; no survival data reported.

Schema field 'tumor_size_measurement' and 'tumor_size_residual_measurement' are not applicable; no tumors assessed.

Biomarker values reported primarily as categorical (increased/decreased) or statistical significance (P-values) rather than quantitative values; absolute fold-changes or concentrations not always provided.
Metabolite measurements performed via LC/MS but specific units (e.g., μM, ng/mL) not explicitly stated for all compounds in the paper text.
Two host species present: human subjects and germ-free mice receiving transplants; normalized to list format.
